To become a U.S. citizen through naturalization, you must meet specific residency and eligibility requirements, file an application, and complete an interview and oath ceremony.

1. Check Your Eligibility

To qualify for naturalization through USCIS, you generally must meet these core requirements:
• Age: Be at least 18 years old at the time of filing.
• Green Card Holder: Be a Lawful Permanent Resident (LPR) for at least 5 years (or 3 years if you are married to and living with a U.S. citizen).
• Continuous Residence: Have lived continuously in the U.S. as a green card holder for the required 3- or 5-year period.
• Physical Presence: Have been physically present in the U.S. for at least 30 months out of the 5 years (or 18 months out of the 3 years if married to a U.S. citizen).
• State Residency: Have lived in the state or USCIS service district where you are applying for at least 3 months.
• Language & Civics: Be able to read, write, and speak basic English, and demonstrate a knowledge of U.S. history and government (with specific age and residency exemptions available).
• Good Moral Character: Show attachment to the principles of the U.S. Constitution and have a clean criminal record free of disqualifying offenses.
• Selective Service: Register for the Selective Service if you are a male aged 18 to 25.

2. Prepare and Submit Form N-400

• Create an account and submit the N-400 Application for Naturalization online or by mail through the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services.
• Pay the required filing fees (discounts or fee waivers may apply depending on filing methods and income).

3. Attend the Biometrics Appointment

• USCIS will schedule an appointment to capture your fingerprints, photograph, and signature for background and security checks.

4. Complete the Interview and Testing

• Attend your naturalization interview at a USCIS office.
• A USCIS officer will review your Form N-400 and test your English skills (unless exempt) and your knowledge of U.S. history and civics by answering questions out of a standard set.

5. Take the Oath of Allegiance

• Once approved, you will attend a ceremony to take the Oath of Allegiance to the United States.
• Surrender your green card in exchange for your official Certificate of Naturalization, which makes you a full U.S. citizen.
